transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2029-03-12 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (CTO - HarborVista), Ethan Park (Eng Mgr), Lena Ortiz (SRE), Marco Silva (PM), Ana Ruiz (Security)

Summary (auto): Kickoff to map HarborVista's conversational traffic into a pilot we can run to validate latency SLOs and cost. Agreed to exchange traffic samples and to run a 2-week focused pilot with replay + synthetic bursts.

00:00 Maya Chen: okay good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. quick round of intros. i'm maya, i'll be your AE.
00:10 Priya Nair: hi i m priya, cto at harborvista, thanks for setting this up.
00:14 Ethan Park: ethan here, engineering manager for the assistant team.
00:18 Daniel Ortiz: daniel from redwood, i'll own the benchmark harness and perf trobleshoots.
00:25 Maya Chen: cool, goal for today is to lock down success criteria and the traffic model so we can build the pilot plan.
00:34 Marco Silva: top concern for us is tail latency during peak chat events — we've seen spikes during promotions where response time jumps.
00:42 Lena Ortiz: and SRE needs to know concurrency per host and what reserve capacity to keep.
00:47 Ravi Patel: thanks. can you sketch the current production numbers? average qps, typical concurrency per session, and typical input/output token lengths?
00:55 Ethan Park: yeah so today's baseline, on our homegrown serving we see about 30 qps sustained for the assistant, with a regular diurnal ramp to 45 qps at peak. we also get short bursts up to 280 qps but those are rare, like 30-90s bursts tied to marketing pushes.
01:12 Priya Nair: average active concurrent sessions around 110 total, which maps to ~6 to 8 concurrent inferences per host on our smallest nodes.
01:20 Daniel Ortiz: useful. what's your token mix? average input tokens and average generated tokens?
01:25 Ethan Park: input tokens average ~72, median 48; generated tokens average 210, 90th ~560, 99th around 2k when customers ask for long summaries.
01:38 Maya Chen: ok that token tail is important — we'll need to define separate SLAs for short vs long generation. e.g., p95 for under 250 tokens, p99 for under 1024 tokens maybe.
01:48 Marco Silva: yes, if the user asks for a 2k summary we don't expect <200ms but we need predictability and graceful degrade.
01:56 Daniel Ortiz: from an infra perspective, do you use kv cache or session caching today? you mentioned a prefix cache in your notes.
02:02 Ethan Park: we do have a small session cache, but it's not consistent across shards — so benefit is limited. we've been thinking about more aggressive prefix caching.
02:10 Ravi Patel: ok that informs batching strategy. for pilot we'll simulate realistic cache-hit ratios: 15% prefix hit, 5% kv-like hits. we'll show delta for 0/15/30% hit models.
02:22 Priya Nair: what about model sizes? currently in prod we're running a tuned 13b variant with integer quant and some custom kernel patches.
02:30 Daniel Ortiz: got it. for the pilot we can test 13b quant and a 7b distilled variant to map cost/latency tradeoffs. we'll also validate quant profiles and kernel selection.
02:40 Ana Ruiz: security question: can you run pilot in our VPC? we need KMS integration, SAML SSO audit logs and to confirm no customer PII leaves our cloud.
02:50 Maya Chen: yes. we support private deployment and VPC pilots. we'll share SOC2 and ISO docs and a KMS integration checklist.
02:59 Marco Silva: what success metrics should we lock?
03:02 Maya Chen: proposing primary success criteria:
- p95 latency < 350ms for responses <= 250 tokens
- p99 latency < 1s for responses <= 1024 tokens
- graceful degradation with fallback model when load > 70%
- no regression in top-10 conversational prompts (we'll run eval suite)

03:22 Ethan Park: can you also include cost per 1M tokens target ? we need unit economics to compare to our in-house baseline.
03:28 Daniel Ortiz: yes we'll estimate cost for hosted vs dedicated pilot and include unit cost projections from the replay.

03:35 Maya Chen: about the benchmark shape — we recommend 3 phases: 1) 1-hour steady-state replay at current sustained qps (30-45 qps) to validate p50/p95/p99; 2) burst staircase tests: repeated 1-minute bursts to 280 qps to measure tail behavior and auto-scale; 3) long-run 24-hour replay to measure cost and token distribution (optional depending on schedule).
03:56 Priya Nair: timelines? we want results before our board meeting in late april.
04:00 Maya Chen: timeline proposal: share benchmark plan by 2029-03-15, ingest traffic sample by 03-18, pilot execution window Apr 8-12, initial report Apr 16, final writeup Apr 23.
04:12 Marco Silva: fits our internal deadlines.
04:16 Lena Ortiz: what about concurrency mapping to GPU sizing? on our end we usually think in concurrency per GPU thread.
04:23 Daniel Ortiz: we'll provide a mapping matrix. preliminary mapping: for the 13b quant profile, expect ~10-14 concurrent short-inference sessions per A100-class GPU equivalent depending on kv-cache hit; for long outputs that drops to 2-4. we'll include GPU concurrency vs qps curves in the benchmark sheet.
04:44 Ethan Park: acceptable. how will you simulate user think-time and multi-turn context growth?
04:50 Ravi Patel: the harness will replay real sessions preserving inter-message think-times and will also synthesize conversation trees for multi-turn growth. we'll parameterize context lengths and show percentiles.
04:59 Priya Nair: about fallbacks — we need a documented policy for automatic downgrade to smaller model on saturation.
05:04 Maya Chen: agreed. pilot will include a canary fallback policy: if tail latency > threshold for 5 consecutive samples, route to fallback model (7b distilled) and log the event. we'll surface the policy in the rollout doc.
05:16 Ana Ruiz: audit logs? we need request-level logs with IDs and safe redaction.
05:21 Maya Chen: yes, request-level tracing and redaction options. we'll share the log retention and KMS key management steps.
05:27 Marco Silva: any competitor gotchas we should be aware of?
05:29 Ethan Park: we've seen Nimbus AI's auto-batching cause spikes in p99 under certain shapes; curious how you avoid that.
05:36 Daniel Ortiz: our runtime uses continuous batching with latency-aware cutoffs and workload-aware routing to prevent pathological batching. we'll demo the cutoffs during the pilot.
05:45 Priya Nair: okay next steps recap?
05:48 Maya Chen: recap: redwood to send benchmark plan, security docs, and cost estimate by 3/15; harborvista shares anonymized 7-day traffic by 3/18; pilot slot apr 8-12; daniel runs harness and uploads results; follow-up presentation apr 16.
06:05 Ethan Park: good. thanks all.
06:08 Maya Chen: thanks everyone, we'll send calendar invites for the pilot kickoff.
